why: Alma 9:15 says 'more tolerable for them' but the Lamanites (9:14) are never mentioned; 9:32 only repeats 9:31
Alma 11:20 opens with 'they received their wages' after Zeezrom's intro; the reader doesn't know who is paid or how

bridges.Alma 11:20: Under Mosiah's law, judges were paid for each day they spent hearing cases, so the lawyers and judges of Ammonihah profited from every quarrel.

why: Zeezrom tells the crowd at 11:35 that Amulek 'said there is but one God', but that exchange (11:28-29) was dropped; 11:42 and 11:45 restate the resurrection teaching of 11:41-44
At 12:7 Alma 'had spoken these words' and Zeezrom sees they know his thoughts, but none of Alma's words to him are shown; 12:3 is exactly that rebuke. 12:10 is repeated in substance by 12:11
Alma 14:22 'many such things did they say unto them' points at taunts the reader never saw (14:18-21)

bridges.Alma 14:22: Day after day, lawyers, judges, and priests came to the prison to question and strike them, taunting them to free themselves if they had such power.

why: Ammon appears at 17:20 without ever being named as one of Mosiah's sons

bridges.Alma 17:20: Ammon, the leader of Mosiah's sons, goes alone to the Lamanite land of Ishmael.

why: At 21:5 'their synagogues' and 'an Amalekite' appear with no introduction; 21:4 introduces the Amalekites and their synagogues. The existing bridge before 21:17 already says Aaron was driven out, so 21:10 is covered
Alma 24:30's lesson about people who 'have been once enlightened' and then fell away points at nothing; the reader is never told the killers were apostate Nephites

bridges.Alma 24:30: Most of the killers were Amalekites and Amulonites, who had once been Nephites. None of them joined the converts.

why: Alma 25:2 seems to destroy Ammonihah a second time, and 25:13 has the Lamanites failing against Nephites the reader never saw them fight

bridges.Alma 25:13: This is the same attack on Ammonihah told earlier. The Lamanites then fought many battles against the Nephites and were driven back each time.

why: Alma 42:2 ends mid-sentence with a dash and 42:4 'And thus we see' has nothing to follow from; 42:3 completes the sentence. 42:21 is not needed between 42:17 and 42:22
Zerahemnah refuses 'an oath' at 44:8 and Moroni refers at 44:11 to 'the conditions which I have proposed', but Moroni's demand (44:5-7) was dropped

bridges.Alma 44:8: Moroni orders them to give up their weapons and swear never to return to war, or be destroyed.
